Rashi on Shabbat 94b:10:1.english: Shreds - Like thin strips that separate from the skin of the finger around the fingernail.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:10:2.english: The majority of which have been severed - [They are] close to being detached.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:10:3.hebrew: מי איכא מידי כו' - כיון דבכלי חייב חטאת, ביד איכא שבות, גזירה אטו כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:10:3.english: Is there any matter, etc. - Since with a utensil one is liable [for] a sin-offering, by hand there is a rabbinic prohibition, [as] a decree lest [one use] a utensil.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:10:4.hebrew: כלפי מעלה - לצד הצפורן התחילו לפרוש, דקא מצערו ליה טפי:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:10:4.english: Facing upward - They began to separate toward the fingernail, for they cause him more pain.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:11:1.english: Due to writing - For she moves a kohl stick around the eye, like a person who moves a reed pen around the letter.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:11:2.hebrew: טווה - שמתקנת שערה בין אצבעותיה ופושטתו כשהוא נכרך. ולשון השני: עושה מאותו בצק כמין חוט:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:11:2.english: Spinning - For she arranges her hair between her fingers and stretches it out while it is wound. And [according to] the second explanation, she makes a kind of thread out of that dough.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:1:1.hebrew: אף במוציא את המת לקוברו - ולא תימא לא פטר אלא במניחו לחוץ, דאין צורך לא לגופו של מוציא ולא לגופה של הוצאה, דאפילו הוא צורך המת, פטור:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:1:1.english: Even one who carries out a corpse to bury it - And do not say that [Rabbi Shimon] only exempts [one] when he leaves it outside, where there is no need either for the sake of the one carrying [it] out or for the sake of the carrying out [itself]; for even [when] it is a need of the corpse, he is exempt.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:1:2.english: A hoe with which to dig - For it is the need of the one who carries [it] out.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:1:3.hebrew: מר לעשות לו טס ולחפור - מרה שנרצף פיו, וצריך להושיב עליו כמין טס דק שיהא ראוי לחפור:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:1:3.english: A hoe, to make a plate for it and to dig - A hoe whose edge was battered, and one needs to fit onto it a kind of thin [metal] plate so that it will be fit for digging.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:1:4.english: To emend [it] and to read [from it]:

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:2:1.hebrew: לאפוקיה לכרמלית - שהיה מוטל בבזיון, או בדליקה, או בחמה. ואי משום טלטול, מניח עליו ככר או תינוק:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:2:1.english: To carry it out to a karmelit - For it was lying in disgrace, or in [the path of] a fire, or in the sun. And if [you are concerned] on account of moving [a corpse], one places a loaf [of bread] or a child upon it.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:2:2.english: A negative commandment - The negative commandment of "you shall not deviate," as [is the case] here.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:3:1.english: One who plucks signs of impurity - [These are] two white hairs through which the bright spot [baheret] renders [one] impure.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:3:2.hebrew: והכוה את המחיה - מחית בשר חי, והוא סימן טומאה בשאת, והכוה זה לבטלה משום מחיה ולטהרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:3:2.english: And one who burned the unaffected flesh - [This is] a patch of live flesh, which is a sign of impurity in a se'et [skin lesion], and this [person] burned it to nullify it from [being] unaffected flesh and to purify it.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:3:3.english: Violates a prohibition - For [it is written:] "Take heed in the plague of leprosy" (Deuteronomy 24).

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:3:4.hebrew: אחד מב' - שלא היו בה אלא שתי שערות, ותלש האחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:3:4.english: One of two - That there were only two hairs in it [the lesion], and he plucked one [of them].

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:3:5.hebrew: חייב - דשקלא לטומאה, שאין מטמאה בפחות מב', דהכי ילפינן לה בת"כ: "שיער" — שנים. וחייב מלקות:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:3:5.english: Liable - Because he removed the impurity, as it does not render impure with fewer than two [hairs], for so we learn it in Torat Kohanim: "hair" [indicates] two. And he is liable to lashes.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:4:1.english: Is it not [that] that which was taught: "He is liable," [is] where he carried out half an olive-bulk from an olive-bulk - For he took it and diminished the [minimum] measure.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:4:2.hebrew: והא דתני פטור דאפיק חצי זית מכזית ומחצה - דאף על גב דמצמצם לשיעור, לאו מילתא היא, ולא אמרינן אהני דאי שקיל מיניה פורתא, תו ליתא לשיעורא:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:4:2.english: And that which is taught: "He is exempt," [refers to where] he carried out half an olive-bulk from an olive-bulk and a half - For even though he reduces [what remains] to the exact [minimum] measure, it is of no consequence, and we do not say that [his action] was effective [in] that if one takes a little bit from it, the [minimum] measure is no longer there.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:4:3.english: From a large corpse - For [his action] accomplished nothing.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:5:1.english: And the same [applies to] his hair - [One who] plucks the hair of his head with his hands.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:5:2.english: And similarly, she who braids - her hair.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:5:3.english: And similarly, one who applies kohl - [to] her eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:5:4.hebrew: וכן הפוקסת - יש מרבותי אומרים: מתקנת שערה במסרק או בידי'. ויש שמפרשין: טחה כמין בצק על פניה, וכשנוטלו מאדים הבשר:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:5:4.english: And similarly, one who applies blush [hapokeset] - Some of my teachers say [that it means] she arranges her hair with a comb or with [her] hands. And some explain [that] she smears a kind of dough on her face, and when she removes it, the skin reddens.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:5:5.hebrew: רבי אליעזר מחייב - בכולם חטאת, וחכמים אוסרין משום שבות. וטעמא דרבי אליעזר מפרש בגמרא משום מאי מיחייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:5:5.english: Rabbi Eliezer deems [him] liable - For all of them [to bring] a sin-offering, and the Sages prohibit [them] due to rabbinic decree. And Rabbi Eliezer's reason is explained in the Gemara, on account of what he is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:6:1.hebrew: מחלוקת ביד - בהא שנוטלן בידו ולא בכלי הוא דפטרי רבנן, שאין דרך גזיזה בכך בחול:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:6:1.english: [The] dispute [is] by hand - It is in this [case], where one removes them with his hand and not with a utensil, that the Rabbis exempt [him], for that is not the manner of shearing on a weekday.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:6:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא בכלי נמי פטרי רבנן - דאין כאן משום גוזז, דלא שייך אלא בצמר בהמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:6:2.english: Lest you say [that] the Rabbis also exempt [one who removes them] with a utensil - For there is no [liability] here on account of shearing, since [shearing] applies only to animal wool.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:7:1.hebrew: מחלוקת לעצמו - בהא הוא דמחייב ר' אליעזר, שיכול לאמן ידו לעצמו לתקנו בלא כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:7:1.english: The dispute is [with regard] to himself - It is in this [case] that Rabbi Eliezer deems [him] liable, since he can steady his hand for himself to trim it without an instrument.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:7:2.english: However, for another - He cannot steady his hand to remove [them] well without a tool.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:7:3.english: It is obvious; we learned "his fingernails" - [Meaning,] his own.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:8:1.english: One who removes [enough] to fill the opening of the scissors - [Enough to] fill the tip of the scissors.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:8:2.hebrew: חייב - בשבת; לרבנן בכלי, לר' אליעזר אף ביד, וזהו שיעורו:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:8:2.english: Liable - On Shabbat: according to the Rabbis, [only] with a utensil; according to Rabbi Eliezer, even by hand; and this is its measure.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:8:3.hebrew: והא תניא - בההיא ברייתא בסיפא, ולקרחה — שהזהירה תורה לא תשימו קרחה (דברים י״ד:א׳) — שתים הוי קרחה; מכלל דפי הזוג לאו ב' שערות נינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:8:3.english: But was it not taught - In the latter clause of that baraita: "And for baldness — [regarding] which the Torah warned, 'You shall not make any baldness' (Deuteronomy 14:1) — two [hairs] constitute baldness." This implies that [the measure of] the opening of the scissors is not two hairs.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:9:1.english: It was also taught thus - Like Rav Yehuda, who said two.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:9:2.hebrew: רבי אליעזר אומר - באחת הוא חייב, ולא בעינן מלא פי הזוג:
Rashi on Shabbat 94b:9:2.english: Rabbi Eliezer says - For one [hair] he is liable, and we do not require the fullness of the opening of the scissors.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:9:3.english: [For] one, he is liable - For he is particular about [even] one [hair], so that he will not appear like an old man.

Rashi on Shabbat 94b:9:4.english: A woman's garment - And it is the way of women to be particular about this and to beautify themselves.

Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:10:1.hebrew: והוא שפירשו כלפי מעלה - פירש בקונטרס: כנגד ראשי אצבעותיו, שהן למעלה כשמגביה ידיו. ור"ת מפרש שכלפי גוף קרי כלפי מעלה, כדאשכחן בפ"ב דנדה (דף יג:) דקאמר "מן העטרה ולמעלה", והתם היינו לצד הגוף:
Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:10:1.english: "And that is if they were severed facing upward" - Rashi explained: [Facing] toward the tips of his fingers, which are upward when he raises his hands. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that [facing] toward the body is called "upward," as we find in the second chapter of Niddah (13b), where it states: "from the corona and upward," and there it means toward the side of the body.

Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:11:1.hebrew: פוקסת - מה שפירש בקונטרס פוקסת היינו סורקת ביד או במסרק — אין נראה, דבגמרא משמע דהוי כעין טוויה, וסריקה אינה כעין טוויה כלל. ועוד, דא"כ היה שונה "סורקת", כדתנן (נזיר דף מב.): "נזיר חופף ומפספס, אבל לא סורק":
Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:11:1.english: Pokeset - That which the Kunteres [Rashi] explained [that] pokeset means combing by hand or with a comb does not seem [correct], for in the Gemara it is implied that it is similar to spinning, and combing is not similar to spinning at all. Furthermore, if so, [the Mishnah] would have taught "soreket" [combing], as we learned in the Mishnah (Nazir 42a): "A nazir may wash [his hair] and part [it], but may not comb [it]."

Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:11:2.hebrew: וכי דרך אריגה בכך - ואף על גב דקולע נימין חשיבא אריגה, כדאמרינן בפרק במה אשה (לעיל שבת ד' סד.), הכא בשער לא חשיבא אריגה כמו בבגד. ועוד, דהכא אין סופה להתקיים, שעומדת לסתירה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:11:2.english: "And is that the manner of weaving?" - Even though one who braids strands is considered [to be performing] weaving, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Ishah (earlier, Shabbat 64a), here, with hair, it is not considered weaving as [it is] with a garment. Furthermore, here it is not meant to endure, since it is destined to be undone.

Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:2:1.hebrew: גדול כבוד הבריות שדוחה את לא תעשה שבתורה - קשה לר"ת, דגבי טלטול דהוי איסורא דרבנן לא שרינן משום כבוד הבריות אלא ע"י ככר או תינוק, כדאמר בפרק במה מדליקין (לעיל שבת דף ל:) ובפרק כירה (שבת דף מג:). ויש לומר, דשאני טלטול דאפשר על ידי ככר או תינוק, לכך לא התיר בענין אחר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:2:1.english: "Great is human dignity, as it overrides a prohibition in the Torah" - It is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: regarding moving [a corpse], which is a rabbinic prohibition, we do not permit [it] on account of human dignity except by means of a loaf [of bread] or a child, as [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (above, Shabbat 30b) and in the chapter [entitled] Keirah (Shabbat 43b). And one can say that moving [a corpse] is different, since it is possible [to do so] by means of a loaf [of bread] or a child; therefore, [the Sages] did not permit [it] in any other manner.

Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:3:1.hebrew: אהני מעשיו דאי משתקלא חדא כו' - באחת מארבע, דאי משתקלא חדא אחריתי נמי לא אזלא לה טומאה — כ"ע מודו דפטור, דהוי כמו חצי זית ממת גדול:
Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:3:1.english: [His actions were] effective, as if one [hair] is removed, etc. - [Regarding plucking] one out of four [hairs], where even if another single [hair] were removed the impurity would still not cease, everyone agrees that he is exempt, for it is like [removing] half an olive's bulk from a large corpse.

Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:4:1.hebrew: והא דתנן פטור דאפיק חצי זית ממת גדול - וה"ה דהוה מצי לאוקמיה כגון דליכא אלא חצי זית בלבד, אלא דניחא ליה לשנויי בחצי זית ממת גדול דהוי רבותא טפי, דאי ליכא אלא חצי זית מן הכל — פשיטא דפטור. ודווקא חצי זית, אבל כזית ממת גדול — חייב; אע"ג דאי משתקלה זית אחר לא אזלא טומאה, מ"מ אהני מעשיו, דמשחתכו לא גריר בתר המת, וכשיוציאו המת מן הבית וישאר כזית זה — יטמא כל הבית, ונמצא שעתה בהוצאה זו הוא גורם טהרה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:4:1.english: And that which we learned [in the mishna]: "He is exempt," [is referring to a case] where he carried out half an olive-bulk from a large corpse - And the same is true that he could have established it [as referring to a case] such as where there is only half an olive-bulk in total, except that it is preferable to him to answer [with the case of] half an olive-bulk from a large corpse, as that is a greater novelty; for if there is only half an olive-bulk in all, it is obvious that he is exempt. And specifically [carrying out] half an olive-bulk [is exempt]; however, [if he carries out] an olive-bulk from a large corpse, he is liable. Even though if another olive-bulk is taken [away], the impurity does not depart, nevertheless his action is effective, for once he cut it off, it is not subsidiary to the corpse, and when they carry out the corpse from the house and this olive-bulk remains, it will render the entire house impure; thus it turns out that now, through this carrying out, he is causing purity:

Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:4:2.hebrew: ממת גדול - לאו דווקא גדול, אלא כלומר מב' זיתים או ג':
Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:4:2.english: From a large corpse - Not specifically large; rather, it means from two olive-bulks or three.

Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:6:1.hebrew: אבל בכלי ד"ה חייב - היינו כרבי יהודה, דמחייב במלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. וא"ת: ודילמא רבנן כר"ש סבירא להו, ומנא ליה דמחייב בכלי? ויש לומר: דא"כ, ליפלגי בכלי להודיעך כחן דרבנן! והא דקאמר "מהו דתימא רבנן בכלי נמי פטרי" — היינו פירושו: דס"ל כר"ש, וכדפרישית. אבל רש"י פירש דפטרי משום דלא שייכא גזיזה אלא בצמר. ואין נראה לר"י, דבהא ליכא למיטעי, דבכל בעלי חיים שייכא גזיזה, כדאמר לעיל: "התולש כנף חייב משום גוזז":
Tosafot on Shabbat 94b:6:1.english: But with a utensil [heading: "he is liable"] - This accords with Rabbi Yehudah, who holds [a person] liable for a labor not needed for its own sake. And if you ask: Perhaps the Rabbis hold like Rabbi Shimon [who exempts for a labor not needed for its own sake], so from where does [Rabbi Elazar] know that [everyone agrees] one is liable [when removing nails] with a utensil? And one can answer: If so, they should have disputed regarding a utensil to convey the far-reaching nature of the Rabbis' [position]! And that which [the Gemara] says, "Lest you say that the Rabbis also exempt [one who removes it] with a utensil" — this is its explanation: that they hold like Rabbi Shimon, as I have explained. However, Rashi explained that they exempt [him] because [the labor of] shearing applies only to wool. But this does not appear [correct] to the Ri, for in this [matter] there is no room to err, since shearing applies to all living creatures, as [the Gemara] said above: "One who plucks a wing [feather] is liable on account of shearing."
